 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of their son D.R. Anjan Gowda S/o Raj Gopal V., in a Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 10.05.2022 at about 5.15 p.m., the son of the Petitioners by name Anjan Gowda was proceeding in his Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA40JA8043 on the left side of the road from Vijayapura towards Devanahalli and when he reached near Yaliyur Cross, Vijayapura Road, at that time, a Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg.
No.KA43M9848 which was driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and in a high speed and dashed behind the Motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, Anjan Gowda fell down and had sustained severe injuries to all over the body and he died in the spot due to injuries.
3. Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Photographer and he was earning of Rs.25,000/ p.m.
The Petitioners entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of D.R. Anjan Gowda, the Petitioners have put to great financial loss SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3655/2022 and mental agony.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg.No.KA 43M9848.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
4. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondents had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.

The Respondent No.1 filed its Objection Statement inter alia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further it contended that this accident took place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle.

Further it contended that the owner of the offending Car Rajgopal vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11644739/
2 bearing Reg. No.KA43M9848 willfully entrusted the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3655/2022 vehicle to the person who did not hold a valid and effective driving licence to drove the same on the date of the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. The Respondent No.2 filed her Objection Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further she contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence and valid Insurance at the time of alleged accident.
Further she contended that the alleged accident took place by the negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, she is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against her.

On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri D.R. Anjan Gowda was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.05.2022 at about 5.15 p.m. near Yaliluru Cross,
Vijayapura Road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru District due to the rash and negligent driving of the Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg. No.KA43M9848 by its driver?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri D.R. Anjan Gowda?

3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
 4) What Order or Award?
 SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3655/2022 7.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.2 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to 10 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence.

8. Having heard arguments by both the sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioners that their son D.R. Anjan Gowda was died in the accident that occurred SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3655/2022 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg. No.KA43M9848.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.2 got examined herself as PW.1 and he has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the averments made in the Petition.
12.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
Ex. P1

and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Santhosh M., S/o Maregowda, the Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg. No.KA43M9848 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar with Sketch which shows that the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3655/2022 concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P5 is the Inquest mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is the PM report which shows the death is due to Polytrauma and injury to brain.

Ex.P7 is the true copy of the ChargeSheet which shows that the I.O of Devanahalli Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending Car for the offences punishable under Sections 279,
304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P8 and 9 are the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners.
Ex.P.10 is the SSLC Marks Card of the deceased.
13. PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.1.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has examined the driver of the offending Car by name Lakshmana Murthy as RW.1.
In the cross examination, RW.1 admitted that the alleged accident occurred SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3655/2022 when the deceased Anjan Gowda was taking his motorcycle to the right turn.
He also admitted that Chargesheet was filed against him and he did not challenge the said Chargesheet.
Further, he admitted that he did not lodge complaint that the alleged accident does not occurred by him.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg.No.KA43M9848 by its driver and in the said accident their son was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
14. Issue No.2

and 3 : Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
15.
It is averred in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the father of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda.

To prove their relationship with SCCH 15 11 MVC Rajgopal vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11644739/
4 No.3655/2022 the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of Petitioners and S.S.L.C. Marks card of the deceased at Ex.P.8 to 10 respectively.

sentences.text: Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda with the Petitioners.
Hence, the Petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda.
16. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 22 years and he was working as a Photographer and he was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
But PW.1 has not produced any document in respect of income.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. Further, the Petitioner has stated the age of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda was 22 years at the time of the accident.
In this regard, PW.1 has produced Ex.P.10 i.e., the S.S.L.C. Marks Card of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda which shows his date of birth was 15.03.1999.
The alleged accident SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3655/2022 was occurred on 10.05.2022.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda was 23 years one month 25 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased D.R. Anjan Gowda to be taken at 24 years for the purpose of assessment.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
19.
The deceased has left behind his parents.
The Petitioner No.1 is the father and Petitioner No.2 is the mother and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3655/2022 No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3655/2022 No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/ to Rs.48,400/.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/ each.

20. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased Anjan Gowda, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/ each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/ towards loss of estate and SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3655/2022 Rupees 18,150/
towards funeral expenses.
IV.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,

5 21.

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents and they had lost their son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
22. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3655/2022 VII.COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:

23. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.15,500/ p.m.
24.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd,

wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "

Held :  yes.
 SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3655/2022  2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40 Upholding bjections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income

sentences.text:
Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork :
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding Rajgopal vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11644739/
6 40 per cent of income for SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3655/2022 future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

entities.text: Rajgopal vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25. The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case person is selfemployed or fixed salary the addition should be 40% below the age of 40 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,500/ comes to Rs.6,200/.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,700/ p.m. (Rs.15,500/ + Rs.6,200/ =
Rs.21,700/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 18.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to held that, if, the deceased was bachelor, SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3655/2022 half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

26. After deducting half towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,700/ it comes to Rs.10,850/
(Rs.21,700/  10,850/) and multiplier applied is 18 which comes to Rs.23,43,600/.
(Rs.10,850/ x 12 = Rs.1,30,200/, Rs.1,30,200/ x 18 = Rs.23,43,600/).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,43,600/ towards loss of dependency.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 96,800/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/

4 . Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.
Loss of Dependency Rs.23,43,600/ Total Rs.25,31,700/ SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3655/2022
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.25,31,700/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

27. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Vitara Brezza Zdi Car bearing Reg.No.KA43M9848.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.

The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2,
has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Rajgopal vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11644739/
7 Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

sentences.text: From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,31,700/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,31,700/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.3655/2022  The Respondent No.1 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% each to the Petitioner No.1 and 2.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively by way of Epayment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively in any Nationalized or SCCH 15 22 MVC No.3655/2022 Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
